items.summary: North Northamptonshire Council is offering additional financial support to households that rely on heating oil as their main energy source. Residents can apply for a £250 voucher in emergency situations where low oil levels would put health, safety, or basic living conditions at risk. The council encourages residents to check online whether they are eligible for the support. Heating oil is not protected by the Ofgem energy price cap, which means households relying on it feel price increases faster than those using mains gas or electricity. Oil prices have been volatile since conflict between the US and Iran began in March, and rural areas such as parts of North Northamptonshire are among the most affected. The government announced a £53m support package to respond to rising costs. Greg Wilcox, executive member for communities and rural affairs, said: "We know that times are hard for many households and we want to do all we can to support as many residents as possible."
items.title: North Northamptonshire Council Offers Heating Oil Support Vouchers

items.summary: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has made a provisional finding that ticket-reselling site Viagogo may have broken the law by failing to show consumers the total price upfront when buying tickets, instead adding mandatory costs such as taxes and booking fees later in the checkout process. This practice is known as drip pricing. The CMA stated it looked into this issue after examining the experience of UK fans purchasing tickets for concerts and sport on three websites operating under the Viagogo brand. It warned that drip pricing can catch consumers out with extra charges, potentially leading them to buy tickets they might not otherwise have selected had prices been comparable from the start. The CMA emphasized that this is an initial finding and it should not be assumed that the company actually broke the law. In a statement, Viagogo said it was cooperating fully with the investigation, which remains ongoing, and added that no final findings have been made. It described its engagement as constructive. This case follows broader CMA activity into online pricing practices; last year it began investigating several companies over the issue, and in August announced that Trainline, Virgin Atlantic, and RED Driving School had engaged in drip pricing. The watchdog can now decide whether consumer laws were broken without going through the courts. For a breach of consumer law, the CMA can impose penalties of up to 10% of global turnover, though it will weigh factors including the severity of conduct before setting the size of any penalty. In June this year, the CMA ordered rival ticket reseller StubHub UK to refund more than 50,000 customers and pay a £900,000 fine for not showing total prices upfront; that company received a 40% reduction in its financial penalty after admitting to breaking the law and settling early.
items.title: CMA provisionally finds Viagogo broke consumer law over hidden fees

items.summary: Actor Ashton Kutcher is expected to become one of Hollywood's most successful technology investors as AI company Anthropic prepares for its initial public offering, which is scheduled for Thursday, November 19. The debut would make him one of the few people to reach billionaire status through business rather than entertainment. His fortune is projected to surge with the IPO, which Bloomberg describes as expected to be one of the largest in history and based on an anticipated valuation of $1.5 trillion for Anthropic. In 2023, Sound Ventures, the venture capital firm Kutcher owns with Guy Oseary, invested $435 million in the company. According to Bloomberg, that stake is now worth roughly $7 billion, representing a gain of approximately 1,500% on the initial investment based on Anthropic's expected valuation at its market debut. Kutcher will not receive this sum directly in cash because it will be distributed among the partners in his firm, which manages outside capital. He has an estimated net worth of $500 million and currently owns a 0.5% stake in Anthropic. Both Kutcher and Oseary decided to invest after meeting with Dario Amodei at the founder's home in Beverly Hills, California, where they discussed AI safety, the company's vision, and the race to develop artificial intelligence over several hours. The article notes that both men had previously seen Anthropic as trailing OpenAI, which Sound Ventures had also invested in; however, this IPO would put Anthropic ahead of OpenAI in reaching public markets. In the first half of the year, Anthropic's revenue surpassed $16 billion, a figure 14 times higher than during the same period a year earlier. Kutcher left Sound Ventures to launch his own venture capital company while remaining involved as a senior adviser, and has also launched another fund in partnership with Morgan Beller. The article observes that it is unusual for actors to attain billionaire status, unlike figures such as Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, Dr. Dre, Tyler Perry, Jerry Seinfeld, Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Irish musician Bono, whose fortunes are linked to the music industry or entertainment ventures like Elevation Partners. Kutcher's return to Hollywood coincides with his starring role in FX's series The Beauty earlier this year after facing criticism for defending Danny Masterson when he was convicted of rape in 2023; both Kutcher and Mila Kunis later retracted their position and apologized to the victims. The article also notes that Sound Ventures has made other lucrative bets, including on Hugging Face Inc., which Nvidia agreed to acquire for $11.2 billion.
items.title: Ashton Kutcher on Verge of Billionaire Status via Anthropic IPO

items.summary:
Drug trafficking, illegal mining, logging and land invasions are intensifying violence and environmental damage across remote Indigenous communities in Peru's Amazon, where criminal groups often operate beyond the reach of authorities. Along isolated borders, expanding cocaine routes are reshaping the rainforest while threatening populations already struggling with a lack of health services and state protection. These concerns came to focus on Sunday as Indigenous representatives gathered in Pucallpa during Pope Leo XIV's visit, hoping international attention would pressure government officials to confront criminal economies operating on their lands.

Global Witness reported in 2025 that it had documented 62 killings or disappearances of environmental defenders in Peru since 2012, including 35 Indigenous defenders. Herlin Odicio, vice president of ORAU, a regional Indigenous federation in Pucallpa, said the group did not want to become part of this statistic and hoped Pope Leo could offer a message that improves government so they can change the system.

An Anadolu report published in August documented how drug traffickers were recruiting Indigenous children to transport cocaine through jungle trails near Peru's border with Brazil. One teenager described being given a revolver and seven kilograms (15.4 pounds) of cocaine paste to carry on a three-day journey. The reporting found that clandestine airstrips, rivers and roads originally opened for oil exploration and logging are facilitating the trade, while a weak state presence including an abandoned border checkpoint has allowed trafficking networks to expand in the Yurua region.

The dangers extend beyond narcotics: illegal mining and logging threaten forests and livelihoods as outsiders take control of land Indigenous peoples have occupied for generations. Naiva Hilda Maringo, an Indigenous representative from Peru's central Amazon, said mining is impacting her community and that animals and plants they depend on are disappearing. Students traveling to Pucallpa raised concerns about land invasions; Italo Bardales, a university student from Atalaya who traveled with more than 350 fellow students representing several Indigenous groups, said outsiders were coming in and taking possession of their territory.

A younger generation of Indigenous leaders is mobilizing around public attention as a way to pressure authorities. Freny Orquia Regatei, an Indigenous Shipibo youth leader from the region, described the visit as an opportunity for these voices to be heard across the world while defending territories and the Amazon.

Ahead of the first-ever papal mass in the Amazon, held at a sports complex in Pucallpa, Pope Leo met with Indigenous leaders, missionaries and church authorities. Speaking before thousands along a waterfront port under a scorching afternoon sun, he addressed deforestation, territorial invasion, a lack of health services and violence against Indigenous leaders and environmental defenders. He condemned drug trafficking for exploiting the poverty of young people and drawing them away from their communities with promises of money. Leo said that in recent years many Indigenous leaders have been murdered for defending their territories.

Bishop of Pucallpa Martin Quijano Rodriguez told Anadolu that Pope Leo's visit sought to draw attention to problems extending across national boundaries, noting the Amazon includes nine countries and concerns the entire world. Born in the US, Leo first arrived in Peru in 1985 as a rural missionary, later serving as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023. His return drew large crowds to Pucallpa, where residents lined the streets to see the popemobile and an estimated 70,000 attended his Sunday afternoon mass.
items.title: Indigenous Communities in Peru's Amazon Face Drug Trafficking, Illegal Mining and Land Invasions Amid Papal Visit

items.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) warns that electricity use by data centres could double by 2030, reaching up to 1,000 terawatt-hours annually under its Stated Policies Scenario. This surge would strain power grids and push global carbon emissions up 70%. The IEA estimates that electricity would account for nearly 30% of global final energy consumption by 2035, compared with 23% in the agency's main scenarios. Peak electricity demand is projected to rise between 40% and 50% by 2035. To keep pace, grids should be expanded by 26 million kilometres of new lines by 2035, while about 16 million kilometres of existing lines would need replacement or refurbishment. The report cites data centre projects in Finland, the United Kingdom, and US states including Texas and Virginia as illustrative cases. It also flags that supplies of copper, transformers, and cables needed for these facilities are already insufficient, with grid spending projected to rise 75% over the next decade. Separately, the IEA notes growing backlash against data centres in the US and Europe over their impact on local communities' public infrastructure, land, water, and energy use.
items.title: IEA Warns Data Centre Power Demand Could Double by 2030

items.summary:
US artificial intelligence company Anthropic, developer of Claude, priced its initial public offering on Wednesday at $81.34 billion based on initial pricing, making it the largest ever recorded that way. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each after expanding its planned offering by 155 million shares and setting the price above the top of its stated range. Anthropic's shares are expected to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, valuing the company at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Of the gross proceeds, roughly $79.38 billion will go to Anthropic from 956.35 million newly issued shares, while existing shareholders sell about 23.65 million shares for approximately $1.96 billion. Underwriters have 30 days to purchase up to 147 million additional shares at the offering price, which could bring total proceeds to $93.54 billion if exercised in full.

Anthropic's initial pricing surpassed SpaceX's June IPO of $75 billion, but SpaceX retains the record for the largest completed IPO at $86.25 billion before fees after underwriters bought additional shares. SpaceX priced approximately 555.6 million shares at $135 each and later sold all 83.3 million additional available shares, bringing its total to 638.9 million shares; it received about $85.68 billion net of commissions and expenses after trading began June 12 under the ticker SPCX.

Before these two US companies went public this year, Saudi Aramco held the record with a $29.4 billion listing in Riyadh that surpassed Alibaba's offering when it listed on Tadawul exchange in December 2019. The government initially offered about 1.5% of the company before an additional share sale brought total proceeds to $29.4 billion, serving as a centerpiece of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030 plan.

Earlier records include Alibaba Group's September 2014 New York Stock Exchange listing that raised $25 billion after underwriters purchased additional shares; SoftBank Group's December 2018 Tokyo listing raising approximately $23.5 billion, though its shares fell sharply on the first day of trading as it funded expansion through the Vision Fund; Agricultural Bank of China's simultaneous Hong Kong and Shanghai listings in 2010 that raised $22.1 billion; Industrial and Commercial Bank of China's 2006 offering raising $21.9 billion after underwriters exercised their option to buy additional shares, marking a milestone in modernizing state-owned banks; American International Group's listing of its Asian life insurance business AIA in Hong Kong in 2010 that raised $20.5 billion and helped repay government assistance from the global financial crisis; and Visa's March 2008 pricing of 406 million shares at $44 each, marking the largest US IPO at the time before ultimately issuing 446.6 million shares for gross proceeds of approximately $19.7 billion and net proceeds of $19.1 billion after trading began on the New York Stock Exchange March 19, 2008.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Becomes Largest in History by Initial Pricing

items.summary: Anthropic, maker of Claude, is set to debut on Nasdaq Thursday in one of history's largest share sales, offering 980 million shares at $83 (€76) each and raising $81.3 billion. The listing values the firm at $1.5 trillion, above market estimates around $1.3 trillion, even as analysts question whether this is optimal timing given recent volatility in AI stocks. Early 2026 saw many AI shares hit record highs on strong earnings from hyperscalers like Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft, but uncertainty grew after the midterms when Democrats took control of Congress and technology stocks fell sharply. The Magnificent Seven lost more than $1 trillion in a single day, and Nvidia's stock plunged nearly 10% over two days following revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy; he resigned, prompting calls from Silicon Valley figures to reinstate him. Analysts remain divided on the IPO: Dennis Dick of Stock Trader Network doubts Anthropic can justify its valuation given current $52 billion revenue versus Goldman Sachs' forecast of more than $600 billion by 2030, while Vivek Seth of Shaires Holdings calls it a once-in-a-generation company whose listing will set a market-clearing price as conditions stabilize. Broader concerns persist about whether AI spending is justified: Goldman Sachs estimated hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their outlays, leaving roughly $230 billion unaccounted for. Capital expenditure plans remain enormous at roughly $800 billion this year, with further $1.2 trillion planned for 2027 and $1.4 trillion for 2028 per Goldman Sachs estimates. Kit Rees of Quilter views the post-election selloff as a healthy correction rather than bubble bursting, noting hyperscalers still plan heavy spending; she suggests watching for signs like slowing AI revenues or reduced appetite for financing through debt or equity offerings. Borrowing costs for CoreWeave and Oracle have risen sharply, and default insurance on Nvidia's debt jumped 76% in a month, yet the four largest firms announced $67 billion worth of new AI bonds since late last month despite Oracle's stock falling 65% from its highs. Gary Smith compares the current boom to earlier manias around railways, automobiles, television and the internet, warning of a potential frightful crash, while Joachim Klement of Panmure Liberum expects any reckoning as early as next year or in 2028.
items.title: Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO amid AI market turbulence

items.summary: Leaders of China, the United States and Russia met for a historic first time in Shenzhen, but the summit produced little new: only non-binding statements on peace and no agreement to meet regularly. In parallel, Europeans gathered in Berlin to demonstrate their backing for Ukraine, described as a pointed response to a summit at which Europe held no seat. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani reported on both developments.
items.title: China-Russia-US Shenzhen summit yields little; Europe reaffirms Ukraine support in Berlin

items.summary: In an editorial for CGTN, Wang Guan rejects the characterization of a recent meeting between the leaders of China, Russia, and the United States in Shenzhen as "Yalta 2.0." He argues that this framing is fundamentally incorrect. According to Wang, rather than repeating history's most infamous power conference, the summit represents something different: an effort at healing divisions, defending the post-World War II international order, resolving conflicts, and safeguarding global energy security. He frames the gathering not as a return to Cold War dynamics but as part of what he calls "a new era of strategic coexistence and constructive competition." Wang concludes that this is Shenzhen 1.0 rather than Yalta 2.0.
items.title: Wang Guan: The China-Russia-US Summit Is Strategic Coexistence, Not Yalta 2.0

items.summary: The term 'hard technology' describes core technologies that are more advanced than high-tech, a concept introduced by Mi Lei, founder of Casstar and an angel investor based in China. When asked why a wave of hard-technology innovation has surged in China, Mi stated: "We need to find a new engine for growth in technological innovation." He added that his team believes hard and core technology will lead the world over the next 30 years.
items.title: Mi Lei on the Surge of Hard Tech Innovation in China

items.summary: A three-day gathering of Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday was billed as historic but is likely to end up a minor footnote rather than the new page in diplomatic history that Putin claimed. The 90-minute meeting offered each leader something to take home: Trump gained proximity to two authoritarian leaders he admires and framed Russia's loss of its Crimean bridge by Ukraine, greeting Putin almost as a wartime ally; Putin was able to show Moscow commands respect from both men while portraying Europe's isolation efforts as failed and the Asia-Pacific region as the centre of the global economy; and Xi used his role as host to signal that American hegemony has ended. The trio issued a brief joint statement covering four disparate topics: boosting energy supply, reforming the United Nations, limiting the powers of the International Criminal Court (ICC), and a tentative commitment to discuss nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation. Putin was most eager to frame the meeting as historic, describing China, Russia and the US as victors of the second world war in what reads as a deliberate slight to Britain, while his pledge to preserve international law seemed aimed at shielding leaders from ICC arrest warrants. The article notes that on the same day the International Court of Justice found Myanmar guilty of genocide for the first time; the Shenzhen statement did not name the ICJ beyond an oblique reference to it and other similar institutions, apparently because its rulings can be dismissed with near impunity. Xi stuck to a familiar script about major powers at peace bringing security while in conflict producing chaos, partly out of nervousness that China's role as protector of the global south might be damaged by involvement in what could become a superpower carve-up. The article acknowledges that serious progress may still be happening behind the scenes on how China might guarantee a peace deal with Iran, who should lead UN reform, and whether Putin can seek peace in Ukraine while protecting Ukrainian sovereignty; for now though it appears the little history made in Shenzhen was made for exclusively the wrong reasons.
items.title: Xi, Trump and Putin summit produced few tangible outcomes

items.summary:
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Berlin to open a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, where he said more than 40 partners would be represented, including President Trump's team. He stated that Ukraine's priorities for the talks are strengthening air defence, energy and financial support, advancing the diplomatic track, and moving toward ending the war while guaranteeing security. Zelenskyy added that Ukraine is doing everything to ensure Europe's full participation in negotiations and planned bilateral meetings with European partners, including Chancellor Friedrich Merz, as well as a format involving American officials and European national security advisers.

The meeting coincided with President Trump holding talks with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Meanwhile, Putin warned that Russia's response to Ukraine's bombing of the Kerch bridge would be "much more painful," after Kyiv attacked the strategic link for the third time this week. He said he had been considering agreeing to local ceasefires until the bridge was destroyed but insisted they would no longer negotiate following the strikes and claimed the bridge was used only by civilians.

Separately, a Russian drone reportedly struck near the Dutch embassy in Kyiv in the mid-afternoon, with reports of explosions heard across the capital. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha confirmed minor damage to one room at the embassy but said no one was injured and urged condemnation of Russia's attacks on foreign diplomats. Dutch FM Tom Berendsen also confirmed a projectile struck behind the embassy, described it as under investigation, and prioritised his staff's wellbeing. The Netherlands' Algemeen Dagblad reported uncertainty over whether the embassy was an intended target or collateral damage from a broader attack.

The incident came shortly after Russia's embassy in the Netherlands asked if The Hague was openly joining the conflict following reports that a Dutch company, Destinus, said its missiles were used in Ukraine's Kerch Bridge strike. Back in Berlin, US peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff described their meeting with Merz and national security adviser Günter Sautter as "very productive," saying they updated them on Trump's discussions in China and continued coordinating positions ahead of the next round of negotiations. Poland's Prime Minister Tusk arrived for talks with Merz, joined at one point by Greece's Mitsotakis, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also attended.

Merz welcomed Dutch PM Jetten after his minority government narrowly avoided collapse over a tax reform dispute, making a dry remark about him being "still alive!"
items.title: Zelenskyy Arrives in Berlin for Coalition of the Willing Meeting Amid Kerch Bridge Strikes and Drone Attack on Kyiv

items.summary: US President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for 90 minutes of trilateral talks in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The leaders had previously held one-on-one meetings but this was their first meeting together, with Thursday's session reportedly originating from Putin. Following the closed-door discussion, the three issued a joint declaration stating that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, pledging to increase petroleum production and supply, commit to reforming the UN, and agreeing that state officials should not abuse immunity while institutions like the International Criminal Court must not overreach their jurisdiction. During separate bilateral conversations before the meeting, Trump greeted Putin as his friend in their first encounter since August 2025 and described his relationship with Xi as very special. The declaration's opening remarks reflected divergent priorities: Xi framed positive interaction among major powers as mandatory rather than optional, while Putin emphasized a shared interest in ending the Ukraine war alongside food and energy security. China has maintained official neutrality on Russia's invasion since 2022, rejecting accusations of tacit support through dual-use technology exports while repeatedly calling for negotiations without condemning Moscow's aggression. Trump stressed that leaders bear special responsibility to maintain dialogue with nations they disagree with, referenced cooperation in preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, and noted prior discussions with Putin on Ukraine, where he expressed hope both sides want an end to the war. Putin described the meeting as an important chapter in diplomatic history but said Ukraine and Europe were not yet ready to compromise, while inviting EU representatives to Moscow; he also vowed far more painful retaliation after Russian forces destroyed a bridge connecting Russia to Crimea's occupied peninsula on Tuesday. The declaration made no mention of nearly five years of Russian attacks on Ukrainian power plants, bridges and residential buildings. Putin drew comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference but argued that reality on the ground must be accepted rather than divided up as it was then. As talks proceeded in China, Kyiv faced drone attacks while Putin held a press conference claiming readiness for peace. The Kremlin released footage of Putin thanking Xi and remarking he did not expect everything to go so well, while CCTV described Xi's assessment of the meeting as positive, constructive and highly productive. Some Russian newspapers characterized the summit as a diplomatic victory following Western attempts to isolate Russia after its invasion began.
items.title: Trump, Putin and Xi issue joint peace declaration after trilateral talks

items.summary: On Thursday, November 19, 2026, China launched the Shijian-24 satellite from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center in Shanxi Province. A Long March-2D rocket lifted off at 6:51 a.m., placing the satellite into its preset orbit. The launch marked the 678th flight mission of the Long March carrier rocket series. According to China's state media outlet CMG, which reported on the event, the Long March-2D is described as highly reliable, cost-effective, and adaptable across various configurations including single-satellite, multi-satellite, and rideshare missions. The rocket can deliver a 1.3-tonne payload to a sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 700 kilometers.
items.title: China Launches Shijian-24 Satellite

items.summary:
The North-East Atlantic Fisheries Commission (NEAFC) met Nov. 10-13 in London, where it failed to reach a breakthrough on how member parties should divide the catch of its three managed stocks: Atlantic mackerel, Atlanto-Scandian herring, and blue whiting. All three have been overfished for years; the Northeast Atlantic mackerel population is currently 22% below the NEAFC's target threshold after being fished above scientifically advised levels every year since 2008. The meeting was dominated by disputes over alleged illegal fishing by Russian vessels, and parties adopted only a statement committing to an ecosystem approach to fisheries management, which NGO observers welcomed as potentially impactful in the long term.

The article explains that many of the most consequential stock decisions actually occur outside NEAFC's remit at parallel "coastal states" meetings. These side deals determine total catch across the Northeast Atlantic ranges of the three stocks, worth billions of dollars; a Pew Charitable Trusts estimate put their collective annual dockside value at roughly 3.5 billion euros or $3.84 billion, mostly from mackerel. In October's coastal states meeting, parties agreed on a 2027 total allowable catch for mackerel of 352,938 metric tons in line with ICES advice; the NEAFC reaffirmed this figure at London but noted it has limited meaning without an agreement on how to divide it. On Sept. 30, ICES forecast that parties would collectively exceed scientific advice for mackerel catch in 2026 by 128%, a gap described as staggering.

NGO observers attribute the failure to share catches partly to these separate coastal states arrangements and partly to geopolitics stemming from Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The other five parties have declined to attend intersessional committee meetings with Russia, holding instead informal like-minded Parties sessions that cannot feed directly into formal processes; the EU suspended NEAFC subsidiary body meetings over this issue. In 2024, the European Union alleged Russian vessels illegally fished with traps and pots in a restricted bottom fishing area known as the "loophole" in the Barents Sea, activity described as ongoing by an unnamed European Commission spokesperson.

At London, parties adopted a measure to limit Russia's mackerel share in NEAFC waters to 1,765 metric tons, less than 1% of total allowable catch, and renewed restrictions on ship-to-ship transfer of Russian-caught mackerel. Four parties voted for it; DFG abstained and Russia voted against. Jonny Hughes of the Blue Marine Foundation said giving Russia roughly 1% is not a real solution because Russia does not currently catch that much.

Beyond these issues, London saw progress on other matters: parties set spurdog catch limits in line with ICES advice, though Jack Renwick of Shark Trust criticized setting them well below scientific advice amid gaps in discard reporting. Parties continued the porbeagle targeted-catch ban for 2027 and 2028; extended vulnerable marine ecosystem bottom fishing closures for five years; and commissioned three independent experts to conduct its first performance review since 2014, with findings expected at the 2027 meeting and a report due in early 2028. The article notes that conservation groups have called for greater transparency, though this reporter had limited access during the first two days of the meeting.
items.title: Geopolitical tensions hamper efforts to curb overfishing in waters near Europe

items.summary: Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London, offered an interpretation of the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held in China. He argues that the gathering is less about reaching concrete agreements or establishing a common position than it is about demonstrating Xi's capacity to convene American and Russian leaders on major geopolitical issues. Li contends that Xi has most to gain from the encounter, as it allows him to project China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. He also suggests Putin may benefit by securing an opportunity to meet both leaders despite Russia's international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine.
items.title: Analyst Frames Xi-Trump-Putin Meeting as China Asserting Diplomatic Centrality

items.summary: The European Commission confirmed on Thursday that it was targeted by a cyberattack conducted using AI tools, marking the first time the bloc reported an attack of this kind. The incident was detected on October 22 and reportedly disrupted several systems for about 10 days before most applications were restored. Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier stated there was no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole, though earlier reporting by Politico suggested large amounts of personal data might have been compromised; the Commission has roughly 33,000 employees. Regnier declined to elaborate on the attack or name a perpetrator but said the institution had taken necessary steps and convened its highest-level internal crisis management body for an urgent meeting in response. Recent hybrid attacks across Europe on supermarkets, air traffic controllers, blood banks, and broadcasters have raised concerns that such incidents may reflect a coordinated effort at hybrid warfare; France summoned the Iranian ambassador last week over cyberattacks that caused supermarket freezers to defrost, though Tehran denied any involvement.
items.title: European Commission Confirms AI-Tool Cyberattack

items.summary:
Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO, which began trading late Thursday on US exchanges, has generated strong interest among Indian retail investors. Although direct participation in US IPO allocations is not permitted for these investors, stockbrokers and specialized investment platforms have introduced pre-order facilities that let them buy shares in the secondary market once Anthropic begins trading. Ashish Kashyap, founder and CEO of INDmoney, said its platform has seen pre-market orders surge about 5x over the past week, with nearly all of that activity driven by bids for Anthropic; he added that average bids are roughly 2X the typical order on the platform. Groww, one of India's largest stockbrokers offering US stocks, opened its own pre-order facility Thursday afternoon and reported significant demand, automatically submitting queued orders to the open market once trading starts. Groww noted that execution depends on market conditions rather than IPO allocation, with an order executed only if the prevailing price is at or below the limit price set by the user.

Anthropic priced its offering at $83 per share across 980,000,000 shares in a listing expected to raise around $81 billion. The debut would be the largest public market entry in history, surpassing Elon Musk-led SpaceX's June listing, and places Anthropic among elite trillion-dollar firms including Alphabet, Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, and SpaceX at a valuation of nearly $1.5 trillion. Founded by former OpenAI Vice President of Research Dario Amodei alongside other OpenAI executives, the company gained prominence through its large language model Claude but has faced multiple controversies, including a standoff with the US government and repeated calls from senior leadership for AI regulation. Prior to this IPO, Anthropic raised $65 billion in Series H funding at a post-money valuation of $965 billion.
items.title: Indian investors flock to pre-order Anthropic IPO shares

items.summary: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on November 18, settling above an earlier range of $70 to $78. Shares were scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19. The company offered 980 million Class A shares in total. Its final prospectus states that retail allocations for investors across the United States and other countries represented less than 20% of the shares offered, a figure that differs from an earlier Yahoo Finance report suggesting up to 20% of an initially proposed 825 million shares could go to retail investors, which would have amounted to as many as 165 million shares. The final prospectus names Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, Trade-PMR, SoFi and E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley among the brokerages involved in distributing shares to retail investors, with Fidelity appearing through two separate broker-dealer entities. Using Fidelity as an example, a minimum request of 25 shares at $83 each would have cost $2,075, though customers holding at least $25,000 in certain assets might be eligible to participate and its offer period was scheduled to close on November 17 at 4 p.m. ET. Fidelity applied a tiered allocation method that considered relationships with the firm based on assets and revenue tied to an account's Social Security number or taxpayer identification number; requesting more shares did not improve ranking, though no more would be allocated than requested. Investors also had to confirm their indication of interest after the price was set, but could still receive fewer shares than requested or none at all even after completing the process. Those who missed out can buy ANT once trading begins on Nasdaq, paying the prevailing market price rather than the $83 offering price; if demand pushes prices higher, buying 12 shares could cost more than $996, while a fall below $83 would make them cheaper. Fidelity also treats selling IPO shares within the first 15 calendar days as flipping, with repeated violations potentially restricting future participation through its platform.
items.title: Anthropic IPO pricing, allocation and post-listing purchase

items.summary:
Anthropic is set to make its Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT on November 19, having priced its IPO at $83 per share with 980 million shares offered. The deal values the company at approximately $81.34 billion. However, the timing of the first trade remains uncertain: while the regular market opens at 9:30 a.m., Nasdaq must collect buy and sell orders through its IPO auction process to establish an opening price, so the first trade may occur well after that time. Alpaca has informed customers that most IPO stocks begin trading between 10 a.m. and noon ET, but this is described as an expected window rather than a confirmed appointment for Anthropic's stock. The article notes that a market order directs a broker to buy shares at the best available price without letting the buyer set a maximum amount they are willing to pay.

Anthropic's debut arrives against a backdrop of a difficult week for US stocks, particularly the Dow and S&P 500. On Wednesday, November 18, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 561.25 points, or 1.1%, to 50,198.17, while the S&P 500 lost 16.90 points, or 0.2%, to 7,323.63 for its fifth consecutive losing session; the Nasdaq Composite rose in contrast, adding 101.50 points, or 0.4%, to 24,429.88. Nvidia (NVDA) remained under pressure despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly earnings: the stock initially gained but reversed its advance and finished down around 2.9%. For the week, the Dow was down 4.1%, the S&P 500 lost 3.1%, and the Nasdaq fell by 2.8%, with uncertainty over AI valuations and returns from massive infrastructure spending continuing to weigh on technology stocks.

Beyond Anthropic, several other events are scheduled for the day. Walmart (WMT) is set to release its third-quarter results before the opening bell, at 6 a.m. Central Time, followed by an investor conference call at 7 a.m. Central. Alibaba, NetEase, PDD Holdings, and Kuaishou will also report quarterly updates or hold earnings calls, offering another look at consumer demand and technology spending in China. The Philadelphia Federal Reserve's November manufacturing survey is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET, alongside initial jobless claims on the economic calendar. Ross Stores and Intuit have further earnings-related events planned after the market closes.
items.title: Anthropic IPO debut timing amid volatile markets

items.summary: JPMorgan analysts Sanjay Mookim and Latika Chopra maintain an overweight rating on Reliance Industries shares, asserting that the rebound in the stock is not yet complete. The brokerage expects earnings momentum to remain positive over the coming quarters, led by strong year-on-year profit growth driven primarily by the oil-to-chemicals business. JPMorgan noted that Reliance could still see further earnings upgrades, particularly for FY28, provided margins hold up, and pointed out that Bloomberg consensus estimates have already been raised materially following the company's quarterly results, though the stock has underperformed relative to the magnitude of those upgrades. In its assessment of the O2C business, JPMorgan expects strong December quarter results; while gasoline cracks have weakened, stronger ethane cracking margins and polyester chain performance, along with lower freight costs, could offset some pressure on refining margins, and falling oil prices may support fuel retailing margins as well. The renewable energy segment was also flagged as an important catalyst, with Reliance's heavy investment in an integrated solar and battery ecosystem at Jamnagar and module commissioning and installation in Kutch expected to draw greater investor attention over the next three quarters. On valuation grounds, JPMorgan said the stock remains supportive relative to the broader market even though its discount to peers has narrowed after the recent rally; at October lows Reliance's retail business was implied to trade around 15 times EV/EBITDA versus roughly double for DMart, whereas current prices imply a multiple of about 30 times EBITDA, approximately 10% below DMart. Finally, JPMorgan anticipates an improving cash flow profile as heavy investment spending fades after three years of materially negative free cash flow; with an EBITDA run rate of around $20 billion annually and management guidance to keep net debt-to-EBITDA below one time, the brokerage expects positive free cash flow despite continued new energy, retail, and petrochemical investments. The Rs 1,675 price target is derived from a sum-of-the-parts valuation using one-year forward EV/EBITDA multiples.
items.title: JPMorgan Maintains Reliance Overweight with Rs 1,675 Target Amid Positive Earnings Outlook

items.summary: Instagram has introduced a feature allowing users to edit their Stories after publishing them, according to Adam Mosseri, head of Instagram. The update lets users modify the text, music, stickers, and drawings in a Story for up to 15 minutes after sharing it on the platform. Mosseri stated that these edits can be made without losing existing views, likes, or replies. He wrote: "If you've ever noticed a typo right after posting a Story, this one's for you." Previously, users had to delete an already published Story and re-upload it to make changes, which could result in the loss of accumulated engagement on the original post. The editing feature is accessed by opening a published Story, selecting the three-dot menu in the bottom-right corner of the screen, and tapping 'Edit Story.' Alongside this capability, Instagram announced several other updates aimed at improving the Story creation experience. These include new fonts, colours, and shapes for stickers; dedicated sticker sheets to make browsing options easier; changes to how users select multiple photographs while creating Stories; and new blur effects, colours, and gradient background options for customising content. The platform described these changes as part of broader efforts to improve its creative tools and make content creation more convenient.
items.title: Instagram Adds Post-Publishing Story Editing Without Losing Engagement

items.summary:
Anthropic, an AI company behind Claude that began trading on the Nasdaq after pricing its IPO at $83 a share above the previously indicated range of $70 to $78, is valued at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis including stock options and restricted stock, or approximately $1.1 trillion on a non-diluted basis. The company was reportedly founded around five years ago. This valuation places it roughly 45% above the combined worth of India's top 10 listed companies, which total about $1.04 trillion, and about 7.6 times Reliance Industries' market capitalisation of approximately Rs 18.46 lakh crore or $197.5 billion. Billionaire banker Uday Kotak noted on X that Anthropic did not exist until around five years ago yet now exceeds the combined value of India's ten largest firms, asking whether Indian companies are undervalued or need to catch up in a new world.

Despite this figure, SpaceX still commands a higher valuation at about $1.9 trillion. The strong pricing signals continued investor enthusiasm for AI stocks even as chipmakers and cloud companies that have committed hundreds of billions of dollars to AI infrastructure face pressure from stretched valuations, rising costs, and concerns over whether the spending will generate adequate returns. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co described the listing as a big win for the tech sector after difficult trading with Nvidia, citing strong demand among investors.

The IPO also brings into focus Anthropic's economics: it has taken on $6.2 billion in debt described by regulatory filings as substantial, remains unprofitable under standard accounting rules, and has committed to spending $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure over the coming years, including $70 billion over the next 12 months. Armina Rosenberg of Minotaur Capital said one listing would not settle the debate about AI economics but that public reporting would become a clear test of whether those economics are holding up.

Anthropic's appeal rests on its focus on enterprise customers and accelerating revenue, which reached $81 billion as of Oct. 31, rising by $10 billion in a single month according to regulatory filings. Goldman Sachs analysts model the company's revenue climbing to roughly $685 billion by the end of the decade. The debut comes amid growing AI competition and uncertainty over whether the spending cycle can continue, including broader market concerns following the sudden exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
items.title: Anthropic's $1.5 Trillion IPO Valuation Outpaces India's Top 10 Firms Combined

items.summary: Two Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) hospitals, KEM Hospital in Parel and BYL Nair Hospital in Mumbai Central, received advanced 3-Tesla MRI machines that were formally inaugurated on Thursday. The event was led by Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde in the presence of Public Health Committee Chairman Harish Bhandirge. Both facilities had experienced significant delays before receiving their equipment. KEM patients faced waiting periods exceeding a month, complicated by frequent machine breakdowns, while Nair Hospital's old MRI unit stopped functioning in 2023 and forced referrals to other facilities such as Sion Hospital. Civic health department officials stated the new machines would enable both hospitals collectively to conduct around 30 to 50 scans daily under one roof on a round-the-clock basis, improving access for emergency and critical patients. The BMC has set a subsidised rate of Rs 2,500 per scan to maintain affordability. Bhandirge noted the equipment would support accurate diagnosis, timely treatment, medical education, and research. He also highlighted that Nair Hospital developed a dedicated MRI department spanning approximately 3,000 square feet, including rooms for the console, reporting, gantry operation, patient waiting, observation, appointments, and seminars. The 3-Tesla technology provides high-resolution imaging of the brain, nervous system, spine, joints, blood vessels, and other organs, with its stronger magnetic field allowing detection of smaller abnormalities that conventional 1.5-Tesla systems may miss. Officials cautioned that actual reductions in waiting times will depend on pending cases, operational hours, and staffing availability. MRI services at Sion and Cooper hospitals are expected to begin soon.
items.title: Mumbai BMC Hospitals Receive 3-Tesla MRI Machines

items.summary: Weeks after an Nvidia scandal came to light, scrutiny has intensified around former executive Ajay 'Jay' Puri and his wife Cenly Chen. Short-selling firm Muddy Waters published a report on Tuesday titled 'Nvidia: More China', which questioned possible links between former Nvidia executives and Super Micro Computer (Supermicro), a California-based server maker facing allegations of illegally diverting products to China. Alongside the report, Muddy Waters shared photos pairing Jay Puri with Cenly Chen, also referred to as Cenly Puri in some images, questioning whether this was the same woman who served as an erstwhile chief growth officer at Supermicro and now heads Chronoscale as CEO, and whether she is the same person named in a lawsuit over chip diversions to China. These identifications remain unconfirmed, and none of the allegations against either individual have been proven. The report also referenced an October shareholder complaint alleging that Chen managed purchases of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) and their customer allocation while being aware of illicit sales to China; Muddy Waters acknowledged these claims still require proof. Regarding its own position, Muddy Waters stated it intended to begin covering a substantial majority or possibly all of its short positions in Nvidia to manage fiduciary risk after the report's publication. Jay Puri had previously been Nvidia's third-highest-ranking executive, behind then-CEO Jensen Huang and CFO Colette Kress, but stepped down from his role as a senior adviser in June after 21 years; he left roughly within a month of Chenly Chen's transition. Their alleged relationship draws scrutiny given their central roles in the AI supply chain. Supermicro responded to South China Morning Post that Chen did not manage its relationship with Nvidia and had no role in deciding how Nvidia GPUs were allotted to customers, adding that she resigned earlier this year to join another company. Despite the revelation contributing to co-founder Huang's departure and investor unease, Nvidia reported strong financial growth on Tuesday, posting quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103 per cent from a year earlier. Nvidia shares jumped more than 5 per cent in after-hours trading on Tuesday, rebounding from a 0.4 per cent dip to $155.46 at the regular close; before that bounce, the stock had shed nearly 17 per cent since the board announced an independent investigation into Huang on November 8.
items.title: Muddy Waters Report Deepens Nvidia China Diversion Allegations Against Jay Puri and Cenly Chen

items.summary: Apple announced a rollout of an all-new Apple Maps experience across India, describing it as faster and more accurate with comprehensive coverage of roads, buildings, parks, shopping centres, and over 300 three-dimensional landmarks. The update introduces Natural Language Guidance that delivers directions in a conversational tone, such as “At the next traffic light, turn left,” alongside real-world detail cues like turning right after a petrol pump. Additional features include Lane Guidance to help users identify the correct lane, multi-stop routing allowing plans for up to 15 stops ahead, and dual-language labels that show place names in both the user's device language and the region's local language. Users can share estimated time of arrival with family and friends through Siri and report accidents, hazards, or speed checks via voice command. The experience also offers interactive street-level imagery captured with high-resolution 3D photography and step-by-step walking directions in augmented reality. Transit support covers riders on buses in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Pune, as well as Indian Railways users who can plan journeys, locate nearby transit stations, and pin favourite routes. The Maps supports English, Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Odia, and Urdu. Dual-language labels and enhanced Natural Language Guidance are available on iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2, and macOS 27.2 or later.
items.title: Apple Rolls Out Updated Maps in India

items.summary: Anthropic raised $81.31 billion in its stock market offering, surpassing SpaceX's previous record of $75 billion and commanding a valuation expected to exceed $1 trillion. The company is scheduled to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT" on November 19, 2026. Its IPO comprises 980 million Class A common shares, of which Anthropic offers 956.35 million while existing shareholders sell the remaining 23.65 million; the company clarified it will receive no proceeds from those shareholder sales. Resident Indian investors who missed the now-closed subscription window cannot buy at the original offer price and instead must wait for trading to begin, purchasing shares at whatever prevailing market price exists, which could mean paying a premium. Once trading starts in the US, they can access Anthropic through overseas brokerage accounts that handle Nasdaq-listed stocks by completing KYC formalities, submitting tax documentation, and transferring funds via an authorised banking channel under the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS). GIFT City-based investment platforms offering US equities are another possible route, though availability depends on each platform's product offerings and regulatory arrangements. Zerodha, Groww, and HDFC Securities are among brokers that offer access to overseas stocks, but investors should confirm whether a chosen platform supports trading in Anthropic shares from the listing date onward. The RBI LRS permits Indian residents to remit up to $250,000 per financial year for permitted purposes such as foreign stock investments, ETFs, travel, and education; this entire allowance can be used for US stocks provided no part of it is needed for other eligible overseas expenses that same year.
items.title: How Indian investors can buy Anthropic shares after its Nasdaq listing

items.summary: Janata Dal (United) raised objections on Thursday after footage surfaced showing a member of Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary's security staff allegedly pushing health minister Nishant Kumar during an official visit to Vaishali district. The incident occurred while the two were reviewing preparations for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's upcoming visit to the area, with Nishant Kumar walking behind Chaudhary when a security personnel pushed him back. JD(U) MLC Neeraj Kumar called the video disheartening and urged Bihar Police headquarters to take cognisance of it and determine whether the push was deliberate or intentional. He emphasized that Nishant Kumar is responsible for Vaishali, noted the pair's close working relationship as remarkable, and warned that those spreading false narratives online would not be spared. Senior JD(U) leader and minister Ashok Choudhary downplayed the matter, stating he believed no security personnel would intentionally push a minister such as Nishant Kumar, suggesting instead that the individual may simply have failed to notice him. Bihar Police's Special Security Group, which provides protection to the chief minister, characterized the incident in its statement as human error committed while its personnel were following established security protocols for Chaudhary. The SSG added that it had provided security to Nishant Kumar for nearly two decades until a few months ago.
items.title: JD(U) demands action over Bihar CM security pushing health minister

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah, addressing the inaugural session of a two-day Anti-Terror Conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in New Delhi on November 19 and 20, called for bringing offenders hiding abroad back to India. He said this was essential to completely eliminate terrorism, organised crime, and drug-related problems, stressing that tackling these threats required coordinated action against criminal networks operating beyond India's borders. Shah argued that offenders based overseas can continue coordinating criminal activities, facilitate cross-border trafficking, and maintain links with associates in India, making international cooperation and extradition crucial. He cited the dismantling of the Popular Front of India (PFI) network as a significant example of coordinated operations by police forces across the country. The Centre banned the PFI and its affiliates for five years under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in September 2022, citing alleged links to terrorist activities, terror financing, and other unlawful acts; the ban followed nationwide searches and arrests carried out by the NIA, Enforcement Directorate (ED), and state police forces. On Jammu and Kashmir, Shah said the Valley was now free of locally recruited terrorists following the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Lateef Bhat, crediting security forces and intelligence agencies for the operation as a significant milestone in eliminating local terror recruitment. The conference theme is cross-border terrorism and brings together state police forces, central agencies, and experts to discuss intelligence sharing, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, digital forensics, terror financing, countering radicalisation, strengthening investigation and prosecution of terror-related cases including use of digital evidence, trial management, witness protection, improving coordination between central agencies and state police forces, and building capacity to respond to emerging security threats.
items.title: Amit Shah Calls for Repatriation of Fugitives Hiding Abroad

The author recounts a flight from Tripoli to Cairo in EgyptAir business class, where he sat next to an American-educated physics teacher at the American University in Cairo who spoke fluent English. After noticing his article about the Nvidia scandal, she observed that this is 'a male-dominated world' in which women never receive credit for seducing powerful men and bringing them down. The author was struck by her point of view and decided to investigate it while flying toward Egypt.

He began with Cleopatra, who in 48 BCE smuggled herself into Julius Caesar's quarters inside a rolled-up bed to become his lover after being unable to pass her brother Ptolemy XIII's palace guards. She regained the Egyptian throne, became Caesar's paramour and bore him a son before later forming an alliance with Mark Antony that ended at Actium in 31 BCE; both died by suicide while Roman propaganda depicted Cleopatra as an oriental enchantress who had emasculated two Roman heroes.

Anne Boleyn is presented next for having made Henry VIII break with Rome, defy the Pope and establish the Church of England to marry her. She failed to produce a male heir, was accused in 1536 of adultery, incest and treason, beheaded, but outlived her influence through her daughter Elizabeth I.

The author then lists Lola Montez, an Irish-born dancer who became mistress of King Ludwig I of Bavaria in the 1840s, gained a title and political influence that provoked public outrage and student protests amid revolutionary turmoil leading to Ludwig's abdication in 1848. He describes Britain's Profumo affair of 1963 involving Christine Keeler, John Profumo, Secretary of State for War, and Yevgeny Ivanov, a Soviet naval attaché; after lying to Parliament before confessing and resigning, the scandal damaged Harold Macmillan's government.

Wallis Simpson is cited as the twice-divorced American socialite who prompted King Edward VIII to abdicate in 1936 amid a constitutional crisis. Mata Hari, executed by France in 1917 on questionable evidence of spying for Germany, became an archetypal femme fatale despite weak proof and possible wartime paranoia.

The author concludes that when a woman influences a king she is called a temptress, but when a man influences a queen he is a statesman; similarly, women persuading rulers are labeled manipulative while men doing the same are politically astute. He argues that because men have traditionally written history books, appointed historians and decided who deserves credit, they received statues and military honours while women were labelled seductresses.
items.title: A passenger's thesis on women and history
